skill.name: obsidian-theme-designer
skill.description: Designs, previews, and generates custom Obsidian themes with visual choices, font pairing, dual-mode colors, and CSS snippet guidance.
skill.summary: Create visual Obsidian theme previews and export an importable CSS snippet.
skill.author: XiangyuSu611

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline CSS variables, normal skill installation paths, and reviewed screenshot images. Confirmed risks remain in the font workflow: external curl downloads, shared temp-directory use, PowerShell registry modification, and a relative helper script command. Additional semantic risks include automatic system font installation and reuse of private vault content in generated previews.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before downloading fonts or changing system font folders. Offer manual install instructions as the default path.
Remove automatic registry writes or replace them with a reviewed manual Windows font installation guide. Never interpolate downloaded filenames into PowerShell commands.
Use a unique temporary directory, validate downloaded files, clean up after installation, and avoid trusting all files in /tmp/fonts.
Ask before using real notes in preview HTML. Default to synthetic sample content and redact sensitive note text when users opt in.
Bundle the helper script or reference a trusted tool explicitly. Do not run scripts/start-server.sh from an ambiguous working directory.

content.value_statement: Custom Obsidian themes often require trial and error in CSS. This skill guides visual choices, previews results, and creates a usable snippet.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes Obsidian appearance settings, installed themes, snippets, and vault structure.
Shows style directions, color palettes, and font options as browser previews.
Builds bilingual previews with headings, quotes, code blocks, tables, tags, and links.
Compares light and dark modes side by side with shared typography.
Generates an Obsidian-compatible CSS snippet after user approval.
Provides steps for enabling the snippet in Obsidian settings.
limitations: Requires access to an Obsidian vault folder for accurate previews.
Font installation commands may need manual review and operating system permission.
Browser previews depend on the referenced visual companion tooling.
Generated CSS may need adjustment for uncommon community themes or plugins.

use_cases.title: Personal Vault Refresh
use_cases.description: Create a cleaner light and dark theme for daily notes, projects, and reading workflows.

use_cases.title: Research Workspace Styling
use_cases.description: Design an academic look with readable typography, tables, blockquotes, and mixed Chinese and English content.

use_cases.title: Team Theme Prototype
use_cases.description: Preview several visual directions before sharing a consistent CSS snippet with collaborators.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Simple Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Design my Obsidian theme. Please ask me simple questions and show visual options before creating the CSS snippet.

prompt_templates.title: Match A Visual Reference
prompt_templates.scenario: User has a preferred app, site, or screenshot.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this reference image as the design direction for my Obsidian theme. Keep it readable in light and dark modes.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Fonts And Colors
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants specific typography and palette exploration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three Obsidian theme variants with different font pairings and color palettes. Include Chinese and English preview text.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Complete Snippet
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for final theme output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my vault appearance, preview the final design, then generate an Obsidian CSS snippet with import instructions.

output_examples.input: I want a dark academic Obsidian theme for research notes.
output_examples.output: The skill presents academic, minimal, dark immersive, cyberpunk, and warm texture directions. It then previews dark academic colors and font choices.

output_examples.input: Make my vault easier to read in Chinese and English.
output_examples.output: The skill compares bilingual font pairings, shows mixed-language sample notes, and recommends a readable heading, body, and code font set.

output_examples.input: I approved the preview. Help me install it.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a CSS snippet, explains where it belongs in the vault, and lists the Obsidian settings steps to enable it.

best_practices: Share a reference image or app style before choosing colors and fonts.
Review previews in both light and dark modes before approving the snippet.
Inspect any font installation command before allowing system changes.
anti_patterns: Do not approve a CSS snippet before seeing a full vault-style preview.
Do not use private note content in demos unless you are comfortable storing it in preview files.
Do not run font installation commands without checking the source and destination paths.

faq.question: Does this skill require CSS knowledge?
faq.answer: No. It guides choices visually and creates an Obsidian CSS snippet after approval.

faq.question: Can it design both light and dark themes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can preview light and dark modes side by side with matching typography.

faq.question: Does it support Chinese and English content?
faq.answer: Yes. The preview guidance includes bilingual headings, paragraphs, numbers, code, and tags.

faq.question: Will it install fonts automatically?
faq.answer: The skill includes font installation commands, but users should review and approve them first.

faq.question: Can it work with existing Obsidian themes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect installed theme variables and generate a snippet that overrides selected styles.

faq.question: What tools does it depend on?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude Code workflows and references visual companion and frontend design tooling.
